thought.text: Clean state, ports consistent, 1.3GB free. Now one final `just serve` (all three) with heap caps, leveraging the now-cached builds:

reasoning_content:
State is clean: nginx is rendered for 39001/39002/39003, ports.json is consistent, all ports are free, 1.28GB is free. Now I'll run a single `just serve` for all three, specifying a heap cap. Each Node process is capped at a 1024MB heap → 3× ~1.2GB + esbuild ~400MB×3 + container ~3.3GB ≈ 8GB... this is still too much. Hmm.

Let me actually count the observed values: when app+boards are running at steady state: app build process ~2GB, boards ~2.2GB, esbuild total ~600MB, container ~3.3GB → ~8.5GB > 7.6GB. With a 1024 heap cap: each dev server's node main process is ~1.1GB → total 3.3GB + esbuild 600MB + container 3.3GB ≈ 7.2GB — right on the edge but should fit (there's also 2GB of existing swap, of which 1.9GB is already used... total swap is only 2GB).

Wait, there's already a 2GB swap partition (/dev/sdc) that's nearly full (1.9G used). So total virtual memory = 7.6 + 2 = 9.6GB, of which ~1.9GB is already in use. Effectively ~7.7GB is available. With heap caps, 7.2GB is borderline... OOM risk is moderate, but this time the build is cached (much faster → less memory retention, shorter overlap).

Alternative plan: run the three sequentially (as before, it worked every time) and keep them running; the risk is that starting the 3rd will OOM the running 2nd. Previously: app(1.1GB avail) + cms(662MB avail) + boards → boards build succeeded, but then the app got killed (during the boards build, when memory was tight at ~900MB avail, the app was OOM-killed... actually dmesg showed 2 OOM kills: 267574 (1.6GB) and 290624 (2.1GB) — one was cms, and one was the app that died during the boards build).

With heap caps + cached builds, each server should stay at ~1.1-1.3GB. Sequential startup: app (~1.2) → cms (~1.2, ~2.5 total) → boards (~1.2, ~3.7 total) + container 3.3 + other 0.6 = 7.6. Right on the edge.

I'll try a single `just serve` (all three) with heap caps. With cached builds, all three builds should finish in ~2-3 minutes with low peak memory. If something gets OOM-killed again, I'll fall back to the state of 2 out of 3 frontends + a complete backend (which I'll report honestly).

action.command:
cd /workspace
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
rm -f /tmp/serve-final.log
setsid nohup env NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=1024" bash -c 'exec just serve < /dev/zero' > /tmp/serve-final.log 2>&1 &
echo "serve pid $!"
sleep 20; tail -2 /tmp/serve-final.log
